title: Demonstration of a Monolithic and Fully Telecom-Fiber-Compatible Tunable Source of Polarization Entangled Photon Pairs Based on a van der Waals Material
authors: Benjamin Laudert, Fatemeh Abtahi, Duk Choi, Dragomir Neshev, Falk Eilenberger
abstract: We present a tunable, single-mode-optical-fiber-based source of polarization entangled photon pairs for the near-infrared telecommunication band that is deployable in standard infrastructure. The photon pairs are generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in a submicron-scale thin film of the inversion-broken rhombohedral polytype of the transition metal dichalcogenide molybdenum disulfide (3R-MoS$_2$), located between two fiber connectors. By exploiting the intrinsic symmetries of the second-order nonlinear susceptibility tensor of 3R-MoS$_2$, this hybrid approach offers control over the generated two-photon polarization state through the incident pump polarization. Most notably, two of the four maximally entangled Bell states, as well as fully co-polarized pairs can be produced. This represents a substantial improvement in terms of tunability and simplicity over established fiber-integrated sources, which require additional optical elements, precise alignment, or careful engineering of design parameters. Additionally, a nonlinear drop in the background photoluminescence signal of 3R-MoS$_2$ is observed at low pump powers, allowing us to reach a coincidences-to-accidentals ratio (CAR) of $(8.3\pm1.8)\times10^{3}$, the highest value recorded for SPDC in van der Waals materials to date.
summary: The research presents an innovative method to generate polarization-entangled photon pairs using $	ext{3R-MoS}_2$ integrated directly within standard optical fibers. By exploiting the material's nonlinear properties and coupling it with precise polarization control, the authors achieve deterministic tuning of the entanglement state in the telecom band. This development is crucial for realizing practical, long-distance quantum key distribution systems.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a highly tunable, compact, and fully integrated source of polarization-entangled photon pairs compatible with standard near-infrared telecommunication optical fiber infrastructure.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated deterministic control over the generated two-photon polarization state by manipulating the incident pump polarization within an in-line $	ext{3R-MoS}_2$ thin film, achieving high entanglement fidelity and a record Coincidences-to-Accidentals ratio.
method: Polarization-resolved coincidence measurements are used to map the generated two-photon state $|\psi_Gangle$ as a function of pump polarization angle ($\varphi_P$) and retardance ($\delta_P$).
model_or_system: The system utilizes Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC) in a submicron $	ext{3R-MoS}_2$ thin film placed directly between standard fiber connectors. The physics relies on the second-order nonlinear susceptibility tensor ($\chi^{(2)}$) of this van der Waals material.
key_observables: Coincidence rates ($I_{HH}, I_{DD}, I_{RR}$), entanglement fidelity ($\mathcal{F}$), concurrence ($C$), and the Coincidences-to-Accidentals ratio (CAR).
important_parameters: Near-infrared telecom band operation ($\sim 1560 	ext{ nm}$), pump wavelength ($\lambda=780 	ext{ nm}$), and polarization control parameters ($\varphi_P, \delta_P$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on modeling the state evolution using unitary transformations derived from fiber birefringence measurements, assuming a self-consistent description of the entire optical network.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup for polarization tuning (using controllers and splitters), show coincidence rate mappings confirming state tunability based on pump parameters, and display density matrix estimations comparing measured states to target Bell states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform ($	ext{3R-MoS}_2$ in fiber) to detailing the measurement techniques (polarization tomography via coincidence rates), deriving the relationship between these rates and fundamental source parameters ($\varphi_P, \delta_P$), and finally demonstrating state control by mapping measured results onto theoretical entangled states like Bell pairs.
why_interesting: This work represents a significant engineering advance in quantum optics, moving entanglement sources from complex free-space setups into robust, chip-scale, fiber-integrated components suitable for real-world quantum communication networks.
